A recent article in our region was misleading about the facts related to nutrition assistance and support for local farmers. So let’s set the record straight: 

While the article focused on farmers market vouchers, it failed to mention that the Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) Program—which those vouchers were designed to supplement, not replace—is on track to receive a $100 million funding increase in FY2026. Those dollars go directly to local farmers and producers.

🔹 The Commodity Supplemental Food Program (meals for seniors) is increasing from $338.6 million in FY2025 to $425 million in FY2026, an $87 million increase.

🔹 The WIC Nutrition Program—the USDA’s largest nutrition initiative—is increasing from $7.6 billion to $7.7 billion, a $100 million increase.

These are real, meaningful increases that directly benefit local farmers and families in need.

Meanwhile, the Citizens Voice article focused on a small, supplemental voucher program that was never intended to be a primary funding source. While the Farmers Market Nutrition Program is being reduced by $8.5 million, that reduction is offset tenfold by a $100 million increase to the core WIC program—which supports the same families in a far more substantial and reliable way.

Reporting focused on a supplemental program while ignoring a substantial funding increase is classic misdirection and disingenuous. So don’t be misled—funding for nutrition assistance is going up, not down. Local farmers should not worry, despite fearmongering from many Democrat leaders and the press.
